findings.summary: Soundness: the inventory lists cited instruction-like files, not every prompt surface of the instance
findings.evidence: `inventory` sees only the paths that claims and rationale cards cite, so a prompt file the study never cites can never appear. That does not meet the request's 'inventories every prompt surface'. `is_prompt_surface` counts any .md/.txt/.prompt/.tmpl file as a prompt, plus any name containing 'agents', 'skill', 'claude' and similar. From the citations in claims.json, the real study's inventory should be AGENTS.md, docs/agent-control.md, docs/architecture.md and docs/configuration.md; the last two are probably ordinary documentation. bin/fm-spawn.sh is left out, although claim c3 in the study says it 'renders a brief', which is an agent prompt. The repo already reads a study's pinned source tree (MountedTree and the pinned-source/ mount, rules.rs:1837-1848). Better: walk the whole pinned tree when the mount is present, recognise known agent-instruction conventions (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .claude/, skills, prompt templates and briefs written inside scripts), treat other .md files as non-prompts unless a study marks them, and test on a small sample tree.

findings.summary: The empty-inventory negative case is tautological
findings.evidence: an_empty_inventory_is_detected only asserts `inventory(&[], &[]).is_empty()`. The non-empty check sits inline in another test, so no test shows it rejecting an empty inventory. Moving the per-instance check into a helper and calling it on an empty result would fix this.

findings.summary: Scope: the test is not where the deliverables list put it, and one file outside the list was changed
findings.evidence: The deliverables list crates/athena-core/tests/prompt_inventory.rs. The candidate puts the test under crates/athena-cap-study/tests/ instead; its doc comment explains that athena-core cannot depend on the study crate, and the reading allowed either place. xtask/shard-timings.txt is not on the list; the change registers the new test file, which looks like this repo's convention.

findings.summary: The changelog and mechanism text describe a narrower property than the requirement
findings.evidence: Both say 'every instruction file a study cites', while the requirement is 'every prompt surface' of the instance.

summary: The candidate adds `inventory` in crates/athena-cap-study/src/prompts_inventory.rs, gives OLY-B-S2-01 a mechanism, owner Athena and a measure ending `status: not shown`, and adds a test in crates/athena-cap-study/tests/prompt_inventory.rs. I ran that test and all 5 cases passed; Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and full-test runs also passed. It fails on soundness. The request asks that Athena inventory every prompt surface of a studied instance. The code lists only the files a study happens to cite, and counts any .md/.txt/.prompt/.tmpl file as a prompt. On the real study, citations I read show docs/architecture.md and docs/configuration.md (probably plain documentation) would be included. bin/fm-spawn.sh would be left out, even though claim c3 in the study says it renders a brief, which is a prompt. A prompt file the study never cites can never appear. The repo already has a way to read a study's pinned source tree (MountedTree and the pinned-source/ mount), but the inventory ignores it. Also, the empty-inventory negative test only checks that the function returns an empty list for empty input; it does not show the per-instance check failing. Smaller issues: the test file is in a different place than the deliverables list said, with a reason given in its doc comment, and xtask/shard-timings.txt was changed outside the list.
